messages:
anya-pm: quick heads-up: big customer (VaultHealth) signed a narrow addendum requesting timely audit exports + a 100ms p95 latency SLA for a subset of endpoints. they want commitment in 2 weeks. we need to rebalance the sprint. thoughts?
jordan-sales: they signed, legal countersigned yesterday. revenue is tied to the SLA milestone in the contract (Q2 payout). they will accept CSV export MVP + streaming stabilization for the SLA subset.
kevin-eng: technical reality: streaming stability fix and audit export are both non-trivial. streaming investigation requires kernel and batching changes; audit export needs safe storage + redaction checks. we can do one fully and make the other an MVP.
mira-cs: customers pushing for audit export for compliance audits. they said latency SLA is critical for customer-facing flows though. CS says split approach might work (audit MVP first, then iterative latency work).
liz-qa: QA note: we have a flaky repro for the streaming regressions. need a dedicated canary test harness to validate p95 improvement. canary takes a day to spin up.
anya-pm: proposal: prioritize audit export MVP behind a feature flag for VaultHealth + start a parallel streaming spike (2 engineers, 3 days) to narrow root cause. then decide mid-sprint whether to reallocate for a hotfix rollout.
sam-design: audit UI isn't required for MVP, but we should ship a small admin page with a download button. I can do the minimal mock in 1 day.
kevin-eng: capacity breakdown if we go that route: 40% audit backend + export hooks, 30% streaming spike + infra, 20% canary/test automation, 10% admin UI + polish. Delivery timeline: audit MVP in 9 dev-days; streaming fix unknown — spike outcome will determine next steps.
oleg-sre: streaming SLA work needs infra reservations. I can reserve a dedicated worker pool in the canary region; that'll cost us capacity but isolates risk. also recommend tracing and token sample retention for 72h.
jordan-sales: VaultHealth expects a go/no-go update by EOD Friday so they can plan their rollout. can we commit to the audit MVP timeline?
kevin-eng: yes we can commit to an audit CSV MVP in 2 weeks if we keep scope strict (truncated prompt column, hashed_user_id, timestamp, model, outcome). no search or UI filtering v1.
mira-cs: legal asked for explicit opt-in from VaultHealth admin before enabling export. will handle agreement language.
anya-pm: decision time: A) Audit-first (deliverability + contract) + streaming spike, B) Streaming-first to chase SLA then audit later. recommend A to protect customer revenue. objections?
liz-qa: choose A, but add mandatory canary gating for audit export to ensure no PII leakage. QA will sign off before download enablement.
sam-design: A works. will deliver admin download page and code for opt-in toggle.
kevin-eng: agree with A. will create the tickets and mark streaming as a prioritized spike with explicit exit criteria: reproducer, performance numbers, and rollback plan.
oleg-sre: I'll prepare the canary pool and tracing. Deploy bot: scheduled canary window 2026-04-03T02:00Z.
deploy-bot: note: deploy window for canary operations is 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC.
jordan-sales: i'll inform VaultHealth and set expectations. they want a weekly status note.
anya-pm: summary: lock on option A. Sprint charter: 1) Audit export MVP behind canary + opt-in (deliver CSV, truncation+hashing, admin toggle, legal opt-in). 2) Streaming spike (2 engs, 3 days) with tracing and canary pool reserved. Acceptance criteria: audit download works in canary for VaultHealth; QA sign-off on PII redaction; spike yields reproducible test and recommended fix.
kevin-eng: I'll open tasks, link to infra ticket, and ping reviewers. PR template: include canary flag and rollback steps.
anya-pm: no objections by EOD -> lock. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
kevin-eng: creating tickets now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/4999
anya-pm: locked. will update roadmap and sprint board.
deploy-bot: reminder: full prod deploy window 2026-04-09 22:00 UTC.
